title: The goal is the whole question
hook: Read the goal first. Every choice is true to the notes, so only the goal decides.

steps.prompt: On a notes question, what should you read first: the notes or the goal?
steps.answer: The goal in the question. Every choice is accurate, so the goal decides.

steps.prompt: Match each goal to what the right sentence must include.
left: Introduce a person to an unfamiliar audience
Explain why something is called a name
right: Who the person is and why they matter
steps.why: The goal's verb tells you what the sentence must do.

steps.prompt: Goal: emphasize how tough tardigrades are.
choices: Tardigrades are usually under 1 millimeter long.
Tardigrades can survive extreme cold, heat, and the vacuum of space.

steps.prompt: Goal: contrast the Amazon and the Nile. Sort each sentence.

cards.text: The Nile is often called the longest river, while the Amazon carries the most water.
The Amazon flows through South America.

steps.why: A contrast names a difference between both things.

steps.prompt: Read the notes fast. Then answer.
show: Wheatley was born in West Africa around 1753.
She learned English, Latin, and Greek.
In 1773 she published a book of poems.
It was the first poetry book by an African American woman.
choices: The book was the first of its kind by an African American woman.
steps.why: Goal: emphasize the book's significance. Only one note says why it matters. Notice you didn't need to remember most of the notes; the goal points to one.

steps.prompt: Goal: introduce Maria Tallchief to readers who don't know her. Which is best?
choices: Maria Tallchief, an Osage Nation member, became the New York City Ballet's first prima ballerina in 1947.
In 1949, she danced in The Firebird.
The Osage Nation is a Native American tribe.
steps.why: An introduction names the person and says who they are.

keys: Read the goal first; every choice is accurate.
The goal's verb (contrast, introduce, emphasize, explain) says what to include.
An introduction names the person or thing; a contrast names a difference.

recall.prompt: Goal: emphasize a similarity. The right choice:
All four choices on a notes question are usually:
What decides the answer on a rhetorical synthesis question?
recall.answer: Whether the choice accomplishes the stated goal.
